purpose: tinycbor is a low-overhead CBOR parsing library for embedded C streams

functions.cbor_encode_undefined: `cbor_encode_undefined()` writes the CBOR **undefined** simple value (major type 7, simple value 23) to the given `CborEncoder`. Use it when you need to emit a CBOR undefined item. It returns the result of `cbor_encode_simple_value()`, so it reports any encoder/error state from that helper.
functions.cbor_value_begin_string_iteration: Begins chunked iteration over a text/byte string `CborValue`. Use it only on a string value and only once before iterating chunks. It asserts on non-strings or if iteration is already active, then delegates to the internal iterator setup.
functions.cbor_value_is_valid: `cbor_value_is_valid()` checks whether a `CborValue*` is non-NULL and not marked `CborInvalidType`. Use it as a quick guard before reading/advancing a CBOR value. It returns `false` for NULL or invalid values, `true` otherwise.
functions.cbor_value_dup_byte_string: `cbor_value_dup_byte_string` duplicates the current CBOR byte string into a newly allocated `uint8_t*`. Use it only when `value` is a byte string; it asserts that. It fills `*buffer`, sets `*buflen`, and optionally stores the next item in `*next`.
functions.cbor_encoder_init: Initializes a `CborEncoder` to write CBOR into `buffer` with capacity `size`. Set `flags` as needed. It sets start/end pointers and initializes `remaining` to 2. Use it before encoding; it doesn’t encode anything itself.
functions._cbor_value_decode_int64_internal:
Decodes the stored integer payload from a `CborValue` that’s already known to be an oversized integer or float/double. Use internally after checking flags/type. If `IntegerValueIs64Bit` is set, it reads 64 bits; otherwise it reads 32 bits.
This is an internal decode routine and should not be called directly. It assumes parser-established invariants, including that flags correctly describe the encoded integer width and that source.ptr has enough backing bytes. Use public parsing/accessor APIs instead, and never set CborIteratorFlag_IntegerValueTooLarge or related flags from untrusted input.
functions.cbor_value_leave_container:
Leaves a container after iterating it. Use `it` as the container iterator and `recursed` as the saved child iterator, which must be invalid. It copies the child’s final position, advances past the break byte for unknown-length containers, then prepares `it` for the next item.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Only call cbor_value_leave_container(parent, recursed) after the iterator returned by cbor_value_enter_container has been fully consumed and is at the end of the container. In TinyCBOR, this means advancing recursed until cbor_value_at_end(&recursed) is true, so that recursed->type becomes CborInvalidType as required by the function's assertion. Do not call cbor_value_leave_container immediately after inspecting just the first element.
functions.cbor_value_validate: `cbor_value_validate` checks that the CBOR item at `it` is well-formed under `flags`. It copies the iterator, validates via `validate_value`, and doesn’t advance `*it`. If `CborValidateCompleteData` is set, any unread trailing bytes cause `CborErrorGarbageAtEnd`; otherwise returns `CborNoError` or the validation error.
functions.cbor_value_get_half_float_as_float: Reads a CBOR half-float and converts it to `float`. Call with a `CborValue*` pointing at a half-float and a valid `float*` output. It asserts if `cbor_value_get_half_float()` errors, then stores the decoded value and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_get_tag: Returns the tag number from a `CborValue` that is already a tag. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_tag(value)`; otherwise the assert fires in debug builds. On success it writes the tag to `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_text_string: Encodes a CBOR text string into `encoder` from `string` with explicit `length`. It’s a thin wrapper over `encode_string` using the text-string major type. Use it for UTF-8 text data; behavior/error handling follows `encode_string` and the encoder state.
functions.cbor_encode_simple_value: Encodes a CBOR simple value into `encoder`. Pass a `uint8_t` simple-type code; it rejects reserved/invalid values in `[HalfPrecisionFloat..Break]` with `CborErrorIllegalSimpleType` (unless checks disabled), otherwise delegates to numeric encoding.
functions.cbor_encode_text_stringz: Encodes a NUL-terminated C string as a CBOR text string. Use it when you already have a `const char *`; it computes `strlen(string)` and forwards to `cbor_encode_text_string`. Behavior depends on that call, so `string` must be NUL-terminated.
functions.cbor_value_get_uint64: Gets an unsigned integer from a `CborValue`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer(value)` is true; it asserts that in debug builds. It writes the decoded value to `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_error_string: Returns a human-readable message for a `CborError`. Use it to report/log errors. `CborNoError` gives `""`; known errors map to specific strings; unknown/unsupported values fall back to `"unknown error"`.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_advance: Pretty-prints the CBOR item at `*value` to `out` using default formatting, then advances `*value` past that item. Use it when iterating over a CBOR stream. It returns the error from `cbor_value_to_pretty_stream`.
functions.cbor_value_to_json: `cbor_value_to_json` is a convenience wrapper to print a CBOR value as JSON to `FILE *out` without advancing the caller’s iterator. It copies `*value` and calls `cbor_value_to_json_advance`; the original `CborValue` stays unchanged.
functions.cbor_value_copy_byte_string: Copies a byte string out of a `CborValue`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_byte_string(value)` is true. It delegates to `_cbor_value_copy_string`, filling `buffer`, updating `*buflen` with needed/copied size, and optionally setting `next` to the following item.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty: `cbor_value_to_pretty` prints a CBOR value in human-readable form to `out`. Pass a valid `FILE*` and a `CborValue*`; it copies the value, so the original isn’t advanced. It returns the result of the pretty-printer, including any parse/IO error.
functions.cbor_value_skip_tag: `cbor_value_skip_tag()` advances a `CborValue` past any CBOR tag(s) at the current position. Use it when you want to ignore tags and reach the tagged item. It loops over consecutive tags, returns the first error from advancing, or `CborNoError` if none/after all tags are skipped.
functions.cbor_value_get_string_length: Returns the length of a definite CBOR text/byte string. Use only after checking the value is a string; it asserts that. If the length is unknown, returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. If it won’t fit in `size_t`, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`; otherwise `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_finish_string_iteration: `cbor_value_finish_string_iteration()` finalizes an in-progress string iteration. Call it only after `cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end(value)` is true. It asserts that precondition, then delegates to `_cbor_value_finish_string_iteration(value)`.
functions.cbor_value_is_byte_string: `cbor_value_is_byte_string()` is a simple type check for a `CborValue`. Use it to test whether the current value is a CBOR byte string before reading it as one. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborByteStringType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_int64: Returns a CBOR integer as `int64_t`. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_integer(value)`. It writes the decoded value to `*result`; if the CBOR item is negative, it converts from CBOR’s encoded form (`-n-1`). Always returns `CborNoError` here.
functions.cbor_encode_tag:
`cbor_encode_tag` writes a CBOR tag header for `tag` using `encoder` without changing array/map element counts. Use it before encoding the tagged item. It returns the underlying encode status; on error, nothing is guaranteed to be written.
Yes—this crash is due to misuse of the encoder state passed to cbor_encode_tag, not a bug in tag encoding itself. Only call cbor_encode_tag with a CborEncoder that was correctly initialized and whose mode matches its initializer: use cbor_encoder_init() for buffer-backed encoding and cbor_encoder_init_writer() for writer-backed encoding. Do not pass attacker-controlled or arbitrary flags to cbor_encoder_init(); use only documented encoder flags so the internal union is interpreted correctly. Ensure the encoder object is zero-initialized or freshly initialized before use, and do not mix buffer-mode and writer-mode operations on the same encoder unless created through the proper TinyCBOR container APIs.
functions.cbor_value_calculate_string_length:
Calculates a CBOR string’s byte length without copying it. Pass a valid `CborValue*` and `size_t*`; it sets `*len` via `_cbor_value_copy_string(..., NULL, len, NULL)`. On error, the returned `CborError` indicates failure and `*len` may remain `SIZE_MAX`.
Misuse: call this only when the CborValue refers to a byte string or text string. Before invoking, check `cbor_value_is_byte_string(value) || cbor_value_is_text_string(value)`. Also ensure `value` comes from a successful `cbor_parser_init` or valid container traversal, and do not call it on a zeroed/invalid iterator after parser initialization failure.
functions.cbor_encoder_get_buffer_size: Returns how many bytes the encoder has written into `buffer` so far: `encoder->data.ptr - buffer`. Use it after encoding to get the used buffer size. It assumes `buffer` is the start of the same output buffer.
functions.cbor_encode_byte_string: Encodes a CBOR byte string into `encoder`. Pass the raw bytes and their length; it writes a definite-length byte string item. It returns the `CborError` from `encode_string` (e.g. success, invalid encoder/output errors).
functions.cbor_value_copy_text_string: `cbor_value_copy_text_string` copies the current CBOR text string into a user buffer. Use it on a `CborValue` that is a text string; it asserts that precondition, then delegates to `_cbor_value_copy_string`. `buflen` is in/out for buffer size, and `next` gets the next item if requested.
functions.cbor_value_get_next_byte: Returns the parser cursor: the next unread byte in the CBOR input. Use it to inspect/peek where `CborValue` will read next. It simply returns `it->source.ptr`; no validation, side effects, or advancing.
functions.cbor_value_is_tag: `cbor_value_is_tag()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` when `value->type == CborTagType`, otherwise `false`. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR tag before reading tag-specific data.
functions.cbor_value_enter_container:
Creates a child iterator positioned at the first item inside a container. Use it after confirming `cbor_value_is_container(it)`. For indefinite-length containers it sets `remaining=UINT32_MAX`; for definite ones it reads the length, and maps count as 2× items. Errors on oversized lengths, leaving `recursed` at the original position.
After cbor_value_enter_container(&it, &recursed) succeeds, iterate through the nested container with cbor_value_advance or equivalent recursive traversal until cbor_value_at_end(&recursed) is true. Then, and only then, call cbor_value_leave_container(&it, &recursed). Also check all return values while advancing nested elements to avoid leaving the iterator in a partially consumed state.
functions.cbor_parser_init_reader: Initializes a parser for an external/streamed source via `ops` and `token`. Set up `parser`/`it`, mark external source, then preparse the first value. Use when data isn’t in a contiguous buffer. Returns `preparse_value(it)`’s error/status.
functions.cbor_value_get_text_string_chunk: Returns one chunk of a text string. Use it only on a text-string `CborValue`; it asserts that precondition. It fills `bufferptr`/`len` with the chunk data and `next` with the next item, and delegates to `_cbor_value_get_string_chunk`.
functions.cbor_value_get_int: `cbor_value_get_int` extracts a CBOR integer into `int`. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true. It writes the converted value to `*result`; if the CBOR item is negative, it returns `-(n+1)`. Always returns `CborNoError` here.
functions.cbor_value_advance:
Advances a `CborValue` iterator to the next item. Use it on a valid, non-invalid iterator. If `remaining == 0`, it returns `CborErrorAdvancePastEOF`; otherwise it delegates to recursive advance logic and returns its `CborError`.
Use cbor_value_advance() as the general-purpose iterator step when the current item may be variable-sized or non-fixed. Prefer this API unless you have already established that the current item is fixed-width. Also avoid passing manually fabricated CborValue structs; only pass iterators obtained from tinycbor parsing APIs.
Call this only when the iterator is known to reference a valid CBOR item (it->type must not be CborInvalidType). Before advancing, ensure parser initialization or container entry succeeded, and stop using the iterator after any fatal parse error. Prefer guarding calls with prior success checks and avoid advancing values obtained from failed initialization paths.
functions.cbor_value_map_find_value: Finds a map entry by UTF-8 text key. Call with a map and key string; `element` is set to the matching value. It enters the map, scans key/value pairs, skips tags, compares text keys, and returns the value pre-parsed. If no match, it returns an error.
functions.cbor_value_validate_basic:
`cbor_value_validate_basic` is a lightweight sanity check for a `CborValue`. It copies the iterator and calls `cbor_value_advance()`, so it does **not** modify the original. Use it to verify that the current value can be advanced past; it returns the advance error, if any.
Call this only on a CborValue produced by a successful cbor_parser_init/cbor_parser_init_reader or valid container traversal API. Do not invoke it after parser initialization fails, and do not use it on iterators that may be invalidated or left uninitialized. Check the returned CborError from parser initialization first.
functions.cbor_value_is_null: `cbor_value_is_null` is a tinycbor type-check helper. Use it with a valid `CborValue*` to test whether the current item is CBOR `null`. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborNullType`; otherwise `false` (including undefined/other types).
functions.cbor_value_get_half_float: Returns the raw 16-bit half-float payload from a `CborValue`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_half_float(value)` is true. It just copies `value->extra` to `result`; otherwise the debug asserts fire.
functions.cbor_value_get_array_length:
Returns the length of a CBOR array when it’s known. Use only on array values; it asserts if `value` isn’t an array. If length is indefinite, it returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. If the length won’t fit in `size_t`, it returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`; otherwise `CborNoError`.
Only call this on a CborValue obtained from tinycbor parsing APIs (for example after cbor_parser_init / cbor_value_enter_container), not on a manually fabricated iterator. Ensure cbor_value_is_array(value) is true and cbor_value_is_length_known(value) returns true before calling. Do not modify value->type, value->flags, value->extra, or value->source.ptr by hand.
functions.cbor_value_is_negative_integer: Checks whether a `CborValue` is an integer encoded as CBOR negative integer. Use it on a parsed value to test type. Returns true only if `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true and the negative-integer flag is set; otherwise false.
functions.cbor_value_at_end: `cbor_value_at_end()` checks whether a `CborValue` iterator has no remaining items in the current container. Use it to stop iterating arrays/maps. It returns `true` when `it->remaining == 0`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_text_string_equals: Checks whether a CBOR value is a text string equal to a NUL-terminated C string. It skips leading tags, returns `*result=false` if not a text string, and otherwise compares chunk-by-chunk via `iterate_memcmp`. Errors from tag skipping/comparison are returned.
functions._cbor_value_get_string_chunk: Returns one chunk of a CBOR string without advancing the input value. Pass a `CborValue*` in `value`; `bufferptr`/`len` receive the chunk, and `next` gets the updated iterator (or a temp if NULL).
functions._cbor_encoder_get_buffer_pointer: Returns the encoder’s current write position in the output buffer (`encoder->data.ptr`). Use it to inspect or continue writing at the current buffer pointer. It just returns the stored pointer; no validation, allocation, or state changes.
functions.cbor_value_is_text_string: Checks whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR text string. Use it to test the item’s type before reading it as UTF-8 text. Returns `true` only when `value->type == CborTextStringType`; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_double: `cbor_encode_double` writes a CBOR floating-point item as a 64-bit double. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and the value to encode. It just forwards to `cbor_encode_floating_point`; errors come from that helper (e.g. encoder/buffer issues).
functions.cbor_encode_uint: Encodes a CBOR unsigned integer into the given `CborEncoder`. Use it for non-negative `uint64_t` values. It delegates to `encode_number(...)`, so it returns a `CborError` if encoding fails (e.g., invalid encoder/output space issues).
functions.cbor_parser_init: Initializes a `CborParser` and the first `CborValue` iterator for a CBOR buffer. Set `buffer/size`, parser flags, and call it before reading values. It zeroes the parser, points to the buffer, sets the iterator to the start, and pre-parses the first item; returns a `CborError` if parsing fails.
functions._cbor_value_begin_string_iteration: Marks a `CborValue` as iterating string chunks. Call before reading a chunked string. If the string length is unknown, it advances to the first chunk; otherwise it just sets the iterator flags. Always returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_get_int_checked: `cbor_value_get_int_checked()` safely extracts a CBOR integer into `int`. Use it on an integer `CborValue`; it returns `CborNoError` on success, or `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if the value can’t fit in `int`. Negative values are handled carefully before conversion.
functions.cbor_value_get_type: `cbor_value_get_type()` is a simple accessor for a `CborValue`’s decoded type. Pass a valid `CborValue*`; it returns `value->type` cast to `CborType`. No parsing or side effects—just reports the current item type stored in the iterator/value.
functions.cbor_encode_floating_point:
Encodes a CBOR floating-point value as half/float/double. `fpType` must be one of those 3, and `value` must point to the matching raw bit pattern type (`uint16_t/uint32_t/uint64_t`). It writes the CBOR type byte plus payload; then appends to the encoder buffer.
This crash is caused by misuse of the API. Call cbor_encode_floating_point() only with fpType equal to CborHalfFloatType, CborFloatType, or CborDoubleType. Do not pass CborSimpleType, CborInvalidType, or arbitrary values cast to CborType. Also ensure the value pointer matches the selected type exactly: uint16_t* for CborHalfFloatType, uint32_t* for CborFloatType, and uint64_t* for CborDoubleType. If the type is fuzz-derived or untrusted, validate it before calling the function and skip or map invalid values to a supported floating-point type.
functions._cbor_value_dup_string: Allocates and duplicates the CBOR string at `value` into a new NUL-terminated buffer. Use `buffer`/`buflen` outputs; `next` gets the following item. First it queries length, then allocates, then copies. Returns OOM or copy errors.
functions.cbor_value_is_map: `cbor_value_is_map()` is a simple type check: it returns true only when `value->type == CborMapType`. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR map before map-specific handling. It doesn’t validate contents or null pointers.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_advance_flags: `cbor_value_to_pretty_advance_flags` is a thin wrapper to pretty-print a `CborValue` to a `FILE*` using `cbor_fprintf`, then advance `*value` as it consumes data. Use it when you want formatted output and iterator progression. It returns the underlying `CborError`.
functions.cbor_encode_float_as_half_float: Encodes a `float` as CBOR half-precision (16-bit) float. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and a `float` value; it converts via `encode_half()` then writes with `cbor_encode_floating_point()`. Returns the encoder’s `CborError`.
functions.cbor_encode_float: Encodes a CBOR float (major type 7, 32-bit). Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and a `float` value. It forwards to `cbor_encode_floating_point`; returns the underlying `CborError` if encoding fails.
functions.cbor_encoder_close_container_checked: `cbor_encoder_close_container_checked()` is just a thin wrapper over `cbor_encoder_close_container()`. Use it to close a nested CBOR container with the parent encoder and the container’s encoder. It returns whatever `cbor_encoder_close_container()` returns; no extra checks or behavior.
functions.cbor_value_is_integer: `cbor_value_is_integer()` is a simple type check: it returns true iff `value->type == CborIntegerType`. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` currently represents an integer before reading it as one. It doesn’t validate range or decode anything.
functions.cbor_value_dup_text_string: `cbor_value_dup_text_string` duplicates a CBOR text string into a newly allocated `char*`. Use it on a value that is already a text string; it asserts otherwise. `buffer` gets the copy, `buflen` its size, and `next` the following CBOR item if requested.
functions.cbor_value_get_byte_string_chunk: Gets one chunk from a byte string, mainly for iterating over chunked/indefinite byte strings. Call it only on a byte-string `CborValue`; it asserts otherwise. On success it returns the chunk pointer/length and, if `next` is given, the next value to continue iteration.
functions.cbor_value_advance_fixed:
Advances a `CborValue` iterator past one fixed-size item. Use only when `it->type` is a fixed type. If `remaining==0`, it returns `CborErrorAdvancePastEOF`; otherwise it calls the internal advance logic.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. cbor_value_advance_fixed() must only be called when the iterator points to a fixed-width CBOR item and the CborValue is a valid parser-produced iterator. Before calling it, ensure the value was initialized by cbor_parser_init()/container traversal APIs, is not at end, is not CborInvalidType, and satisfies the fixed-type precondition (for example by checking the item kind and only using cbor_value_advance_fixed for simple fixed-size scalar types). For non-fixed items such as containers, strings, tags, or unknown-width values, call cbor_value_advance() instead.
functions.cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer: Checks whether a `CborValue` is an integer and not marked negative. Use it to test for CBOR unsigned integers before reading as `uint*`. It returns `true` for non-negative integers, `false` for negatives or non-integers.
functions.cbor_encode_boolean: Encodes a CBOR boolean into `encoder`. Pass `true` or `false`; it maps to CBOR simple values via `cbor_encode_simple_value()`. Returns the underlying `CborError` from that call, so it can fail if the encoder can’t write.
functions.cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size: Returns the size of the current string chunk while iterating a chunked CBOR string. Use only when `value` is in string-chunk iteration mode (`CborIteratorFlag_IteratingStringChunks`); otherwise the assert fails. It fills `*len` and returns a `CborError`.
functions._cbor_value_extract_int64_helper:
Returns the integer payload from a `CborValue`. Use it internally when you need the stored 64-bit value: if `IntegerValueTooLarge` is set, it decodes via `_cbor_value_decode_int64_internal()`, otherwise it returns `value->extra` directly.
This is an internal helper and should not be invoked or relied on directly by external code. Prevent crashes by using only public accessor APIs on parser-initialized CborValue objects and never constructing inconsistent flag/extra/source state manually.
functions.cbor_value_get_raw_integer: Returns the CBOR integer’s raw unsigned 64-bit encoding. Use only on integer `CborValue`s; it asserts if not. On success, stores the extracted value in `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_is_boolean: `cbor_value_is_boolean()` is a quick type check for a `CborValue`. Use it to test whether the current item is a CBOR boolean before reading it. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborBooleanType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_reparse: `cbor_value_reparse` refreshes a `CborValue` iterator by reparsing the current/next item. If the iterator is in string-chunk mode, it does nothing and returns `CborNoError`; otherwise it calls `preparse_next_value_nodecrement(it)`. Use it when the underlying buffer/state may need re-evaluation.
functions.cbor_value_is_array: `cbor_value_is_array()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` only when the `CborValue` currently points to an array (`CborArrayType`). Use it to test a parsed CBOR value before treating it as an array; otherwise it returns `false`.
functions._cbor_value_copy_string:
Copies a CBOR text/string into `buffer` via chunk iteration. Pass `buflen` as in/out: on entry max space, on return bytes used/needed. If `buffer==NULL`, it just reports size. `next` gets the position after the string. Returns `CborErrorOutOfMemory` if truncated.
Misuse: this is an internal helper and should not be called directly by external code/fuzz drivers unless all library preconditions are guaranteed. If used, pass only a valid string-typed `CborValue`, a valid `buflen` pointer, and optionally a valid `next` iterator. Prefer public APIs after verifying the type first, and avoid invoking it on non-string, uninitialized, or parser-error states.
functions.cbor_value_is_float: `cbor_value_is_float()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` only when `value->type == CborFloatType`. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` currently represents a CBOR float before reading it as one; otherwise it returns `false`.
functions.cbor_encoder_close_container: Closes a nested CBOR container and syncs the parent’s buffer state. Use it after finishing items in the child encoder. For unknown-length containers it appends the CBOR break byte; for fixed-length it checks item count, returning TooFewItems/TooManyItems, or OutOfMemory if buffer is full.
functions.cbor_value_to_json_advance: Converts the CBOR item at `*value` to JSON and writes it to `out`. Use it when you want to serialize the current parsed value; it passes the value’s type and recursion limit to `value_to_json`. Behavior depends on that helper and returns its `CborError`.
functions.cbor_encoder_create_array: Creates a CBOR array container. Call it with a parent encoder, a child encoder for the array contents, and the item count. It initializes the nested encoder; the returned error reflects setup failure. Use the child encoder to write elements.
functions.cbor_encoder_init_writer: Initializes a `CborEncoder` to use a writer callback instead of a fixed buffer. Pass the encoder, write function, and opaque token. It stores the token in `end`, sets `remaining=2`, and marks writer mode; if `CBOR_ENCODER_WRITE_FUNCTION` is defined, the callback is ignored.
functions.cbor_value_is_container: `cbor_value_is_container()` checks whether a `CborValue` is a container item: it returns true only for arrays or maps, false otherwise. Use it to test an iterator/value before treating it as nested CBOR data.
functions.cbor_encoder_create_map: Creates a CBOR map container encoder. Use it with a parent encoder and a child `mapEncoder`; `length` is the pair count, or `CborIndefiniteLength` for indefinite maps. It returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if `length` is too large, otherwise delegates to container setup.
functions.cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end: Checks whether string-chunk iteration is finished. Use it while iterating a CBOR text/byte string with chunk APIs. It returns `true` when `cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size()` reports `CborErrorNoMoreStringChunks`; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_int64_checked: `cbor_value_get_int64_checked` safely reads a CBOR integer into `int64_t`. Use it after confirming the value is integer; it returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if the CBOR integer exceeds `INT64_MAX`. On success, it writes the signed value, handling CBOR negative integers as `-n-1`.
functions.cbor_value_is_half_float: `cbor_value_is_half_float()` is a simple type check. It returns `true` when `value->type == CborHalfFloatType`, meaning the CBOR item is a half-precision float (16-bit). Use it to test the current `CborValue` before reading it as a half float; otherwise it returns `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_int: Encodes a signed 64-bit integer as CBOR. Pass an initialized `CborEncoder` and the `int64_t` value. It maps nonnegative values to unsigned integers and negative values to CBOR negative integers via complement encoding, then delegates to `encode_number()`.
functions._cbor_value_finish_string_iteration: `_cbor_value_finish_string_iteration()` ends a string/chunked-string iteration. If the string is indefinite-length, it skips the CBOR Break byte; then it advances to the next item via `preparse_next_value()`. Use it after finishing reading string chunks.
functions.cbor_encode_raw: `cbor_encode_raw` appends `length` bytes from `raw` directly to the encoder buffer as raw data. Use it when you already have encoded CBOR or other bytes to inject unchanged. It just forwards to `append_to_buffer`; it returns that call’s `CborError` result.
functions._cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size: Returns the size of the current string chunk in a CBOR string iterator. Use with a valid `CborValue*` and `len` output pointer. It delegates to `get_string_chunk_size`, so it returns that function’s error code and fills `len` on success.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_stream: Pretty-prints a CBOR `CborValue` to a user-supplied stream callback. Pass the output function, token, value, and flags. It just forwards to `value_to_pretty` with max parser recursion; returns that `CborError`.
functions.cbor_value_is_length_known: `cbor_value_is_length_known()` checks whether a `CborValue` iterator points to a definite-length item. Use it before relying on `cbor_value_get_array_length()`/`_map_length()`. It returns `true` when the `UnknownLength` flag is not set, `false` for indefinite-length items.
functions.cbor_value_is_undefined: Checks whether a `CborValue` is the CBOR `undefined` simple value. Use it on a valid `CborValue*`; it returns `true` only when `value->type == CborUndefinedType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_float:
Gets a CBOR float from a `CborValue` into `result`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_float(value)` is true; it asserts that and that the stored integer bits fit the float encoding path. It decodes raw 32-bit data and memcpy’s it into `float`, then returns `CborNoError`.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Do not manually fabricate a CborValue by setting only type/source/remaining and then call cbor_value_get_float(). This function expects a CborValue produced by TinyCBOR parsing APIs, with internal fields and flags initialized consistently. To avoid crashes, first initialize a parser with cbor_parser_init(), obtain a valid CborValue from the parser/iterator APIs, verify the item is a float with cbor_value_is_float(), and only then call cbor_value_get_float(). If constructing test inputs, fuzz serialized CBOR bytes through the parser rather than synthesizing CborValue structs directly.
functions.cbor_value_get_simple_type: Returns the CBOR “simple” value from a `CborValue`. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_simple_type(value)`. It asserts on invalid input, writes `value->extra` to `*result`, and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encoder_get_extra_bytes_needed: Returns how many extra bytes the encoder still needs to finish the current CBOR item. Use it after encoding to check completeness: `0` means done; nonzero means the output buffer was too small and more space is needed.
functions.cbor_value_is_double: `cbor_value_is_double()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` when `value->type == CborDoubleType`, otherwise `false`. Use it to verify a `CborValue` holds a CBOR double before reading it.
functions.cbor_value_is_simple_type: `cbor_value_is_simple_type()` checks whether a `CborValue` currently represents a CBOR simple type. It’s a read-only predicate: returns `true` only when `value->type == CborSimpleType`, otherwise `false`. Use it to test before handling simple values.
functions.cbor_encode_half_float: Encodes a CBOR half-precision float (16-bit). Use with a `CborEncoder*` and `value` pointing to the float data to encode. It just forwards to `cbor_encode_floating_point(..., CborHalfFloatType, ...)`, so it returns that function’s error/result.
functions.cbor_encode_negative_int: Encodes a CBOR negative integer from its absolute value. Pass the magnitude of the intended negative number; it writes `-(absolute_value + 1)` per CBOR’s format via `encode_number`. Returns the encoder’s error status.
functions.cbor_value_get_boolean: `cbor_value_get_boolean` reads a CBOR boolean from a `CborValue` into `*result`. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_boolean(value)` is true; otherwise the debug `assert` fires. It returns `CborNoError` and sets `*result` to true if `value->extra` is nonzero, else false.
functions.cbor_encode_null: `cbor_encode_null()` encodes the CBOR null simple value into the given `CborEncoder`. Use it when you want to write a CBOR `null` item. It returns the `CborError` from `cbor_encode_simple_value()`; pass a valid encoder.
functions.cbor_value_get_map_length: Returns a map’s item count. Use only on a map `CborValue`; it asserts if not a map. If length is indefinite, returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. On success writes `size_t` length; if it won’t fit, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`.
functions.cbor_value_get_double: Returns the CBOR float64 payload from a `CborValue` into `result`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_double(value)` is true; it asserts that and that the stored integer bits are present. On success it bit-copies the 64-bit data and returns `CborNoError`.
